Model optimization for data imbalance was performed. • Deployment tool allows retraining on current data and visualization via heatmaps for dynamic operational guidance in terms of optimal return flows for each treatment trai Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs 47 5.2 BNR: ABAC / AvN + PdNA (Application 2) Water Resource Recovery Facilities (WRRFs) employing Ammonia-Based Aeration Control (ABAC) can sometimes be burdened with outdated unstable control systems that struggle from disturbances occurring in conjunction with long delays. The ammonia control may fail to be precise, forcing staff to overcompensate with large safety factors, potentially leading to inefficiencies that manifest as wasted operating costs. The research at HRSD explores a promising solution: implementing data-driven solutions into the controllers. These tools, including digital twins (DTs) and data-driven models (DDMs), could be a game-changer within existing ABAC frameworks. However, it should still be recognized that there is no such thing as a one-size-fits-all approach. To find the optimal balance between effectiveness and complexity, HRSD tested three different control strategies at three different HRSD WRRFs. The most challenging scenario occurred at the Nansemond Treatment Plant (NTP), which involved rather unpredictable influent loads and plug flow reactor orientation. Here, HRSD experimented with a feedforward-feedback controller that included ML. The NTP case study is presented in this section (Section 5.2). At the HRSD Army Base Treatment Plant (ABTP), a classic feedback Proportional-Integral (PI) controller was employed and proved effective, likely due to a favorable residence time distribution (RTD) resembling something close to a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR). The third facility was the Virginia Initiative Plant (VIP), where influent load was rather predictable, but the RTD was more plug flow. This warranted a more complex feedforward-feedback approach. These latter two control strategies are not featured in this report. 5.2.1 Background (Set the Stage) HRSD employs a 5-stage Bardenpho at their NTP and leverages Ammonia Based Aeration Control (ABAC) to try and maintain a constant ammonia (NHx) concentration leaving the aerobic zone (Figure 5-13). In the figure, flow enters the biological process from the Primary Clarifiers (PCs) and then exits the biological process to then enter the Secondary Clarifiers (SCs). In between the PCs and the SCs are the 5 stages of the Bardenpho, including the Anaerobic (ANA), 1st Anoxic (1 ANX), Aerobic (AER Zones 1-3), 2nd Anoxic (2 ANX), and Re-Aeration (RE- AER) zones. 48
